score_basis: Strong specialized operator uncertainty extension (anchor 4). Scalar digit-weight and Fourier Hamming laws are classical, as now acknowledged; no Millennium-scale claim is supported.

correctness_confidence.basis: All main proof steps A,Z,B-prime,R,N,B checked analytically and attacked at characteristic-two phases, valuation domination, primitive-direction coverage and incidence counts. New targeted exact tests passed.

rigor.basis: Self-contained principal operator proof and careful conditional T3 statement; all-sparsity conjectures are distinguished from theorems. Speculative final extensions need more qualification.

novelty.basis: Scalar law and Radon minimum are known; operator extension through 2p-1 and valuation/primitive-direction mechanism appear credible contributions within bounded source search, without worldwide priority certification.

significance.basis: Useful noncommutative improvement over elementary rank-times-sparsity for some prime-power ranges; applications and general sparsities remain unresolved.

reproducibility.basis: Exact cyclotomic constructions and Clifford tests reproduced; independent polynomial, incidence, phase and gap checks passed. Large exact-sparsity tables and all high-dimensional searches were not replayed.

summary: The exact revised candidate supports Theorem B: every nonzero cyclic Weyl combination with at most 2p-1 terms in dimension p^k obeys the stated nullity envelope. The valuation argument is valid for arbitrary complex coefficients, including p=2 after adjoining 2d-th roots. The new N mechanism is coherent, while Theorems A,Z and Lemma R are correctly attributed to classical literature. Recommend local acceptance; T3 remains conditional and the all-sparsity conjectures are not proved.
strengths: Full primitive-direction family corrects the insufficiency of only p^k+1 directions; conjugated matrices remain integral even though Fourier conjugators are not unimodular.
Lemma R has an elementary characteristic-p proof and Lemma N reduces a hypothetical sparse obstruction to one p-torsion plane.
The scalar law is accurately calibrated against Delvaux–Van Barel and the weight-retaining property against Massey–Costello–Justesen.
Exact sparsity versus monotone support budget, theorem versus conjecture, conditional T3 and historical versus new computation are clearly separated.
weaknesses: Section 8 item 5 suggests a similar argument for order pq, although Section 5.3 explains that the all-roots-to-one valuation does not exist there. This is a speculative research direction, not a consequence of the current proof, and should be phrased accordingly.
The exact composite tables and numerical searches occupy considerable space relative to the principal new theorem; several large entries rely on supplied historical computations not rerun here.
Novelty is bounded: no global literature priority certification, and scalar/Radon ingredients themselves are not new.
potential_errors: No material error found in the principal theorem or its proof. The phrases true envelope beyond ell=p should continue to be read as the conjectured all-sparsity operator envelope, as the later formal statements specify.
strong_novelty_candidates: The rank/nullity law for arbitrary complex combinations of cyclic Weyl operators through sparsity 2p-1 in dimension p^k.
The all-sparsity valuation form B-prime whenever one primitive-direction residue polynomial survives.
The primitive-line obstruction minimum mechanism N and its torsion-coset reduction, subject to bounded prior-art search.
